dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?

Hi, Denise. My name is Sofia Amaral, A-M-A-R-A-L. I'm calling about water that's pooling in the street at 434 Mill Street, up in Historic Hill. I'm on speaker, I've got my hands full, so I hope you can hear me.
I can hear you fine. Go ahead, tell me what's going on.

So, this started with last weekend's nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday. It's Wednesday now, so three days later, and the water has not gone down. It's not draining. There's a big pool right across the crosswalk by the school bus stop, and I'd say it's, um, maybe fifteen feet wide, from curb to well into the lane.
Okay. And that's right at your address, or down the block from it?

It's about two doors down from my building, to be exact. Right in front of 434 is where it begins and then it spreads toward the crosswalk. And the thing is, the kids can't get to the bus stop without stepping through it. This morning, 7:40, I watched four of them. They didn't want to get their shoes soaked, so they were stepping out into the road to go around it. Cars were coming. A delivery van had to swerve.
Oh, that's not good. Especially at that hour, with traffic and kids.

No, it's not. And I'm going to be honest, I'm frustrated, because this is the third day. I walked out Sunday evening, around five, and it was there. Monday it was there. I assumed somebody would come once the storm passed. Nobody has. Nobody came.
Let me get some details so I can send this to the right crew. Is there a storm drain you can see near the water? A grate?

There's a grate at the corner, on the downhill side. I walked over to look, and it's, sorry, I should correct that, it's not at the corner exactly, it's about ten feet up from the corner. It's covered with leaves and, I think, a lot of sand and gravel that washed down. The water is just sitting on top of it.
That sounds like it's clogged with debris. Is the water moving at all, or is it just standing?

It's moving a little, and that's the other thing. It's running along the edge of the street and heading toward my neighbor's garage. It's the one with the low driveway, two houses down. As of about twenty minutes ago the water was maybe six feet from the garage door. If we get any rain, or if it freezes and thaws, I think it's going in there.
Okay, I'm noting that. Water heading toward a garage, and the crosswalk is covered. Have you talked to the neighbor?

I knocked Monday, no answer. I left a note. I don't want to scare anyone, I just don't know who to call to get it checked. Is that you, or is it somebody else? I've been bounced around before, so I'd rather ask first.

No, you're in the right place. Storm drains and street flooding come through Public Works, so I'll put in a work order for a crew to come look at the grate and the street. I can mark it as a safety concern because of the bus stop.
Please do. Mark it however gets it moving. I'd really like a crew out today, if that's at all possible.

I'll flag it as a priority. After a storm like that we've got a backlog, so I can't promise today, but a safety one near a school stop goes to the top of the pile. Realistically you're looking at today or tomorrow.
Okay. Today or tomorrow. I'll write that down. Wednesday the twenty-fifth, ten forty-something a.m., spoke with Denise. Is it okay if I note that?
Absolutely, go ahead. Do you want me to take a callback number in case the crew needs to reach you?
Yes. It's 401-555-0192. That's my cell.
Got it, 401-555-0192. And that's Sofia Amaral at 434 Mill Street.

Correct. And just so you have the full picture, the pool is on the street side. I'm on the second floor, and from my kitchen window I can see the whole thing, and past it, I can see the lighthouse. So I can keep an eye on it and tell you if it changes. That's how I knew it was still there at five Sunday.
That's helpful, actually. A good view of it. Is the water getting any deeper, or is it staying about the same?

About the same since Monday, I'd say. Maybe four inches at the deepest, near the crosswalk line. It's the spreading toward the garage that worries me. And [pause] sorry, the kids. Honestly, that's what I'd like fixed first.
Understood. I'll put that at the top of the note. Is there anything blocking the grate besides leaves, like a branch or trash?
I couldn't see any branch. Just leaves, sand, and some kind of paper, a flyer maybe. Nothing huge. I'm not going to reach in and clear it myself, it's under water.
No, please don't. Stay out of it, especially with cars going by. The crew has what they need to clear it.
Right. Fair enough. And if nobody shows up by tomorrow afternoon, should I call this same line?
Yes, call this number back, and mention the work order for Mill Street. I'll make sure the note says it was reported this morning so you don't have to start over.
Good. Because on Sunday I thought it would sort itself out, and on Monday I thought they'd come, and now it's Wednesday. I'd just like it handled.
I hear you. I'm sending it over right now. You did the right thing by calling.
Thank you, Denise. I appreciate it. I'll watch from the window.
Sounds good. Take care, Ms. Amaral.
You too. Bye.
